title: Trauma in Patients with Psychosis (TriPP) – Traumatisation in People with a Psychosis Diagnosis
summary: Many people with psychosis have had stressful or traumatic experiences. These can lead to separate difficulties known as trauma-related disorders. Because the signs of psychosis and of trauma overlap, this often goes unrecognised. At psychoseambulanz.berlin, the TriPP project examines how common traumatic experiences and trauma-related disorders are among people with psychosis, how often they have been recognised so far, and whether the experiences occurred before, during or after the psychosis. To do this, existing treatment records are analysed. In addition, an English-language questionnaire is tested in German, and a new questionnaire is developed and piloted. Participants complete questionnaires and take part in interviews over up to four appointments. Their treatment is not changed. The aim is to better recognise and treat the consequences of trauma in people with psychosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Parts A, B1 and B2:
• Age 18 years or older
• Diagnosed psychotic disorder (ICD-10: F20–F25)
• Treatment at psychoseambulanz.berlin; for Part A: documented routine clinical data from 2024–2026

Additionally for Parts B1 and B2:
• Sufficient German language skills for questionnaires and diagnostic interviews
• Mentally and cognitively capable of giving informed consent
• Written informed consent to study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Parts B1 and B2:
• Acute psychotic episode or any other condition currently preventing informed consent
• Acute suicidality or any other acute crisis
• Severe cognitive impairment or neurological disorder preventing participation in the assessments

Part B2 only:
• Previous participation in Part B1

Part A:
• No additional exclusion criteria (if applicable: objection to the use of routine data – check against data protection concept)
